attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors represents the product of the magnitude of one vector and the projection of the other vector onto it. Geometrically, it equals |A||B|cos(θ), where θ is the angle between vectors A and B. When the dot product is zero, the vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular), meaning their angle is 90° and there is no projection of one onto the other. A negative dot product indicates that the projection of one vector onto the other points in the opposite direction, corresponding to an angle greater than 90° but less than 180°.

attempts.raw: TEXT The dot product of two vectors measures how much one vector extends in the direction of the other. Geometrically, it equals the product of their magnitudes and the cosine of the angle between them: A·B = |A||B|cos(θ). If the dot product is zero, the vectors are orthogonal (perpendicular), meaning the angle between them is 90° and neither projects onto the other. A negative dot product means the projection points opposite to the direction of the other vector, indicating an angle between 90° and 180°.
